stem.text: The function f is twice differentiable at every x in the closed interval \( [0, 7] \), with \( f'(5) = 0 \) and \( f''(5) < 0 \). Must f attain an absolute maximum value on the open interval \( (0, 7) \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because \( (0, 7) \) is not a closed interval, so the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply there.

worked_solution.text: f is differentiable, and so continuous, on \( [0, 7] \), but the question asks about the open interval \( (0, 7) \).
The Extreme Value Theorem needs a closed interval, so it gives no conclusion on \( (0, 7) \).
The absolute maximum of f on \( [0, 7] \) may occur only at an endpoint, which the open interval leaves out, so f need not attain an absolute maximum value on \( (0, 7) \).

options.label: No, because the Extreme Value Theorem places the absolute maximum of f on \( [0, 7] \) at an endpoint.
options.derivation: the existence theorem used to place the extreme value at an endpoint, which is then read as a verdict
